name: Pupillary Unrest Index
description: Measures pupillary unrest (hippus) — natural pupil oscillations absent in AI-generated faces.
mechanism:
This method analyzes pupillary unrest (hippus) for deepfake detection:

1. **Pupil Size Measurement**: Pupil diameter is measured per frame using iris-pupil boundary detection and ellipse fitting. High-resolution tracking captures the temporal signal of pupil diameter changes.

2. **Hippus Detection**: Pupillary unrest (hippus) is the continuous, involuntary oscillation of pupil diameter at frequencies of 0.5-2 Hz with amplitude of 0.2-0.5mm. This is a normal physiological phenomenon reflecting sympathetic-parasympathetic nervous system interplay. The method checks for the presence and characteristics of hippus.

3. **Pupillary Light Reflex**: When illumination changes, pupils should constrict (light increase) or dilate (light decrease) with characteristic latency (~200ms) and dynamics (rapid constriction, slower dilation). The method checks for correct pupillary light reflex dynamics. Deepfakes typically don't model this physiological response.

4. **Bilateral Pupil Coordination**: Both pupils should show consensual response — constricting/dilating together with minimal difference (≤0.5mm). The method checks bilateral pupil size correlation. AI generators may produce independent pupil sizes between left and right eyes, violating the consensual pupil response.

5. **Cognitive Pupil Response**: Cognitive effort and emotional arousal produce small pupil dilations (0.1-0.5mm above baseline). The method analyzes whether pupil size correlates with speech content complexity and emotional context. Deepfake pupils that don't respond to cognitive demands lack this natural physiological signal.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models
